title: The Galaxy-Cluster Residual in de Sitter-MOND: the Dark Sector Has the Mass, but a Density-Ordering Veto Forbids It from Being Galaxy-Safe and Cluster-Clumpy at Once
description: MOND and its relativistic completions reproduce galaxy rotation curves with one acceleration scale a0 but leave a factor-~2 missing-mass residual in galaxy-cluster cores (Sanders 1999, 2003), shared across the whole relativistic-MOND family. We ask whether this residual is explained WITHIN the de Sitter-MOND framework (a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = cH_Lambda/Z, Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.7888, a0 = 9.36e-11 m/s^2), whose dark sector is the Aether-Scalar-Tensor (AeST) ghost-condensate of Skordis & Zlosnik (2021): a cold, w=0, rho~a^-3 MODE of the gravity field, not a new particle. We report a clean two-sided result. (i) The abundance is NOT the problem: the AeST shift-symmetric Q-mode carries Omega_dm worth of cold density, which at the cosmic dark-to-baryon ratio supplies ~7.0e14 Msun inside R500 against the ~4.79e14 a factor-2 cluster requires -- a ratio of 1.46, with ZERO mass tuning. The framework's dark sector HAS the cluster mass. (ii) But it cannot deploy that mass galaxy-safely: the Q-mode is sound-speed-zero (c_s^2 -> 0) sub-horizon -- the very property that lets AeST fit the Planck third acoustic peak -- so its Jeans length vanishes and growth is gated only by the mass term rho > mu^2/4piG. Galaxy disks and cluster cores both exceed this by ~10^13, AND the galaxy disk is ~3.7x DENSER than the cluster core: the density ordering runs BACKWARDS, so any field that clumps in cluster cores clumps MORE in galaxies. Injecting the required density into a fiducial disk shifts the radial-acceleration relation by +0.12 to +0.23 dex against a 0.11-0.14 dex scatter floor -- re-introducing the cuspy-halo scatter MOND was built to remove. No acceleration gate evades this: a0 is absent from the AeST linear perturbations (Bridge-1), so the dust grows CDM-identically. The conclusion is a no-go, stated symmetrically: the residual IS the framework's own dark sector doing a cold-dark-matter job -- that is the explanation -- but in the two clean field limits the sector either over-fills clusters and breaks galaxies, or stays galaxy-safe and fills only ~17-20% of the core. There is no limit in which it does both. The 'pure MOND, no dark matter' reading is forfeited: the framework contains dark matter, of a non-particle (gravity-mode) kind. A galaxy-safe no-new-particle stack (the Y-Q response +17-20%, intracluster-light/baryons within the cosmic baryon ceiling, budget-capped stellar remnants) closes ~36% of the robust ~1e14 Msun core gap, leaving ~64% open; the core gap is robust (resolved core weak-lensing/X-ray ratio ~1.03, so it is not deflated by the weak-lensing-vs-hydrostatic question). We test the natural scale-selection escape -- a ghost-condensate k^4 Jeans length ordering clustering by scale (clusters yes, galaxies no) -- and find it closed at the linear level: the quadratic higher-derivative coefficient is ZERO in the published AeST action (Blanchet & Skordis 2024, Sec 6.2, verbatim: 'no higher derivative interaction terms in the action, which are also quadratic in the fields'), so there is no k^4 Jeans scale; the one finite scale (the condensate mass mu^-1 >~ 22 Mpc) sits above all clusters with the wrong topology; and even granting a k^4 term the Jeans length scales as rho^-1/4 (shorter in the denser galaxy, re-importing the no-go). The single remaining galaxy-safe lever is therefore the AeST NONLINEAR term's dependence on the gravitational-potential depth |Phi| -- the enhancement Durakovic & Skordis (2024, 'Towards galaxy cluster models in AeST', arXiv:2312.00889) found set by 'the boundary value of the gravitational potential', called 'the potential of AeST to address the shortcomings of MOND in galaxy clusters', and explicitly deferred beyond the isothermal case; it is the only door (across an exhaustive search) that passes both the galaxy-RAR and the Cassini vetoes. We PERFORM that deferred non-isothermal calculation (the +mu^2*Phi Helmholtz mass term in the AeST weak-field equation, solved numerically on real A2029-class cluster baryon profiles; solver validated against analytic MOND at mu->0 to 1e-6) and find the lever genuinely real and large -- ~1e5x the naive coupling, reaching 28-100% of the core residual -- and galaxy- and Cassini-safe at its natural footing (RAR shift 7e-4 dex, Saturn anomaly 1e-9 fractional), but DESCRIPTIVE rather than predictive: the closure is set by the Helmholtz oscillation PHASE, not the cosmological boundary value, so it requires a per-cluster tune (the same cosmological boundary admits eta from -3 to +4; the natural untuned boundary gives a DEFICIT), and the value imposed universally breaks the galaxy RAR by 0.275 dex. The framework's own dS-Unruh inertia is horizon-set and blind to local Phi, so the coupling is AeST's not the framework's; the cluster sector remains irreducibly phenomenological. The single un-closed branch is whether a full 3D cosmological AeST N-body dynamically pins the oscillation phase the static boundary-value problem leaves free -- the only computation that could reopen the door, performed by no author. Two negative results close common escapes: the framework's history-dependent modified inertia is WRONG-SIGNED for a surplus (d ln M_eff / d ln a0 = -1 exactly), and the neutrino (hot-dark-matter) option is excluded by KATRIN (2024) and DESI DR2 (2025). All quantitative claims are reproduced by committed Python scripts (all exit 0) at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula. Quarantine note: a0, Z, kappa, and the dark-sector amplitude I0 are inputs/free parameters, never asserted to be derived. This is a both-sided consistency analysis of an existing theory's dark sector, not a discovery paper and not a claim of a theory of everything.
